newsitem.title: UK: National Power rebounds on positive comment.
newsitem.headline: National Power rebounds on positive comment.

text.p: Shares in British utility National Power Plc rose on Thursday amid positive comment on the company and the valuation of its shares, bouncing back on Thursday from a decline following poorly-received first-half results.
National Power shares were up 6-1/2p at 441-1/2 by 0920 GMT, after on Wednesday falling 18p, and rival PowerGen was also higher to be up 4-1/2p at 583.

The Financial Times Lex column said there was "no compelling reason" for the stock's four percent drop and said "investors can pick up few other manufacturing stocks at prospective price/earnings multiples of eight times."

Separately, a report in the daily Independent newspaper said National Power was in talks with regional electricity companies to create a combined supply business when the market was open to competition in 1998.
It said PowerGen was also in talks with regional electricity companies.

On Wednesday National Power fell after the compay posted a drop in first-half pretax profit before exceptional items to 251 million stg, from 253 million a year before, and said it would pay a 6p dividend, at the low end of forecasts.
